title: Coefficient lifting and finite presentation of a principal formal variety
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete and separated for powers of $(\pi)$, where $\pi\in B$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose $k$ is a characteristic-zero field and a specified homomorphism $k\to B/\sqrt{\pi B}$ makes that quotient a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Here $\sqrt{\pi B}=\{b\in B:b^n\in\pi B\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$. There exist a homomorphism $k\to B$ lifting the specified homomorphism, an integer $r\geq0$, and a continuous surjective homomorphism of $k[t]$-algebras $q:P\to B$, where $t$ acts on $B$ by $\pi$ and $P=\widehat{k[t,x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_{(t)}$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Continuity is for the $(t)$-adic and $(\pi)$-adic topologies. In particular $B/\pi B$ is finite type over the lifted field.

proof.text: If $B=0$, take its unique coefficient map, $r=0$ and the unique map $\widehat{k[t]}_{(t)}\to0$; all assertions hold. Henceforth assume $B\ne0$. Put $J=\sqrt{\pi B}$. By Noetherianity choose generators $z_1,\ldots,z_s$ of $J$ and integers $e_i\ge1$ with $z_i^{e_i}\in\pi B$. For $N=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$, every degree-$N$ monomial in the $z_i$ contains some $z_i^{e_i}$, so $J^N\subseteq\pi B$. If $s=0$ take $N=1$. Thus $(\pi)^n\subseteq J^n$ and $J^{Nn}\subseteq(\pi)^n$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, printed pp.18--19; agent expansion of the coefficient lifting and principal-adic successive approximation arguments. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The two filtrations give the same compatible-sequence ring: given compatible residues modulo $J^m$, its residue modulo $(\pi)^n$ is obtained from the coordinate modulo $J^{Nn}$; conversely take the coordinate modulo $(\pi)^n$ and reduce modulo $J^n$. Compatibility makes the composites identities. Hence $B\cong\varprojlim_m B/J^m$ by the assumed $(\pi)$-adic completeness. Moreover $J$ is proper: if $J=B$, then $(\pi)=B$, so $(\pi)$-adic separatedness would force $B=0$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, printed pp.18--19; agent expansion of the coefficient lifting and principal-adic successive approximation arguments. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every nonzero integer $a$ is a unit modulo $J$, since its inverse comes from the specified characteristic-zero field map. Lift this inverse to $c\in B$ and put $u=1-ac\in J$. The sums $v_h=\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}u^i$ stabilize modulo every $(\pi)^n$, since $u^{Nn}\in(\pi)^n$; completeness gives $v\in B$ with $(1-u)v=1$. Thus $cv$ is an inverse of $a$. Consequently $B$ and every $B/J^m$ have canonical $\mathbf Q$-algebra structures, and the specified map $k\to B/J$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra map (a unital ring map preserves inverses).

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, printed pp.18--19; agent expansion of the coefficient lifting and principal-adic successive approximation arguments. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Construct compatible $\mathbf Q$-algebra maps $s_m:k\to B/J^m$ for $m\ge1$, starting with the specified $s_1$. For the induction step set $D_m=B/J^{m+1}$ and $L_m=J^m/J^{m+1}$. Then $L_m^2=0$ because $2m\ge m+1$, and $D_m/L_m=B/J^m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-formally-smooth] to the field extension $k/\mathbf Q$, the $\mathbf Q$-algebra $D_m$, its square-zero ideal $L_m$, and $s_m$. It supplies $s_{m+1}$ reducing to $s_m$. Their compatible sequence defines $s:k\to\varprojlim_mB/J^m=B$, a ring map whose reduction modulo $J$ is exactly the specified map.

proof.text: Choose $y_1,\ldots,y_a\in B$ whose residues generate $B/J$ over $k$. Let $R\subseteq B$ be the image of evaluation on the finite list $(y_1,\ldots,y_a,z_1,\ldots,z_s)$ over the lifted field. Then $B=R+J$. Each $J^m$ is generated over $B$ by degree-$m$ monomials in the $z_i$, all lying in $R$; replacing each coefficient using $B=R+J$ gives $J^m\subseteq R+J^{m+1}$. Starting with $B=R+J$, induction yields $B=R+J^m$ for every $m\ge1$. At $m=N$ we get $B=R+\pi B$. Hence the images of this finite list generate $B/\pi B$ over the lifted $k$. Rename the list $b_1,\ldots,b_r$.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, printed pp.18--19; agent expansion of the coefficient lifting and principal-adic successive approximation arguments. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $A=k[t,x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and let $e:A\to B$ evaluate $t$ at $\pi$ and $x_i$ at $b_i$, using $s$ on coefficients. For each $n\ge1$, evaluation induces $e_n:A/t^nA\to B/\pi^nB$, since $e(t^nA)\subseteq\pi^nB$. These maps commute with reduction: both composites evaluate the same polynomial modulo $\pi^mB$ for $m\le n$. Applying $e_n$ coordinatewise therefore gives a ring map $q:P=\varprojlim_nA/t^nA\to\varprojlim_nB/\pi^nB=B$. On $A$ it equals $e$, so it is a $k[t]$-algebra homomorphism with $q(t)=\pi$. Also $q(t^nP)\subseteq\pi^nB$, proving continuity for the stated adic topologies.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1 and 3.2.3, printed pp.18--19; agent expansion of the coefficient lifting and principal-adic successive approximation arguments. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $b\in B$ put $c_0=b$. Given $c_j$, choose a polynomial $h_j\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ representing its residue modulo $\pi B$ (Step 5), and choose $c_{j+1}\in B$ with $c_j-h_j(b_1,\ldots,b_r)=\pi c_{j+1}$. Then $H_m=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}t^jh_j\in A$ satisfies $b-e(H_m)=\pi^mc_m$. The classes $H_m\bmod t^m$ are compatible, hence define $H\in P$; the coordinate formula for $q$ gives $q(H)\equiv b\pmod{\pi^mB}$ for all $m$. Separatedness implies $q(H)=b$. Thus $q$ is surjective. No cancellation of $\pi$ was used, so this also covers $\pi=0$ and nilpotent or zero-divisor $\pi$.
